adjacent: 2 lines in a shape that are **immediately next to each other or touching**
algorithm: a procedure used for **solving a problem or performing a computation**
area: a measurement of the **space inside a two-dimensional shape**
Associative Property of Multiplication: the product of 3 or more numbers **remains the same regardless of how the numbers are grouped**
attribute: a **feature or trait** of an object or set of objects
axis (axes): the perpendicular lines that form the coordinate grid, in which the **vertical axis is the line going up and down**/on the left and the **horizontal axis is the line running side to side**/on the bottom (plural: axes)
base: the number **being multiplied by itself** in exponential form
column: a part of an array that **goes up and down**
Commutative Property of Addition: the order in which numbers are added **does not change the sum**
Commutative Property of Multiplication: the order in which numbers are multiplied **does not change the product**
coordinate grid: a grid with **numbers labeling the gridlines**
coordinate: a pair of numbers that represent the **distance from 0 in two directions**, starting on the horizontal axis
cubic unit: any three-dimensional measure of volume that represents a **number of cubes that have a defined side length**
cup: a liquid volume unit in the U.S. Customary measurement system (**16 cups is equal to 1 gallon**)
defining attribute: a trait or property that **a shape must have**
Distributive Property: multiplying the sum of **2 or more addends** by a factor will **give the same result** as multiplying each addend individually by the factor and then adding the products together
dividend: the number being divided, representing the **total number being equally distributed or divided**
divisor: the number that follows the division symbol that represents either the **number of equal-sized groups or the size of each group**
equation: a math statement showing that the **values on each side of the equal sign are the same**
exponent: a number representing the power to which a given number or expression should be multiplied, expressed as a **small raised number** (ex: in the expression 10^4, 4 is the exponent)
expression: a mathematical statement with a **minimum of 2 numbers and at least 1 math operation**
factor: a number that is **multiplied by another number** to determine the product
gallon: a liquid volume unit in the U.S. Customary measurement system (**1 gallon is equal to 4 quarts, 8 pints, or 16 cups**)
hundredths: the base-ten place value unit **equal to 1/100** (one hundredth in standard form is **.01**)
inequality: the name of a statement used to express the relationship between two unequal numbers, in which **< or > symbols** are used
line plot: a display of measurement data in which every data value is shown with a **symbol above a number line**
mile: a unit of length in the U.S. customary measurement system (**1 mile is equal to 5,280 feet or 1,760 yards**)
milligram: a unit of weight in the metric measurement system (**1,000 milligrams is equal to 1 gram**)
millimeter: a unit of length in the metric measurement system (**1,000 millimeters is equal to 1 meter**)
mixed number: a number expressed as a **whole number and a fraction less than 1**
non-unit fraction: a number that describes **more than 1 part of a whole** that has been partitioned into **equal parts**
ordered pair: a pair of 2 numbers that correspond to points on the **x and y axes**, expressed as **(x, y)**
origin: the point where the **2 axes intersect** on the coordinate plane, which is located at **(0,0)**
parallelogram: a quadrilateral with **2 pairs of opposite sides that are parallel and have equal length**
parentheses: grouping symbols that can be used in expressions or equations to indicate the **order in which operations should be performed**
partial product: the value obtained when **multiplying the parts of 2 numbers separately** (which is then added to other partial products to arrive at the total product)
partial quotient: the value obtained when **multiplying the divisor in a division equation by another number, then subtracting that number from the dividend** (which is then added to other partial quotients to arrive at the total quotient)
perpendicular line: a line that crosses another line at a **90° angle**
pint: a liquid volume unit in the U.S. Customary measurement system (**8 pints is equal to 1 gallon**)
plot: to place a point (often representing **x and y coordinates**) on a grid
product: the value when **2 or more numbers are multiplied**
quadrilateral: a polygon or shape with **4 sides and 4 angles**
quart: a liquid volume unit in the U.S. Customary measurement system (**4 quarts is equal to 1 gallon**)
quotient: the result obtained by dividing 2 numbers representing either the **number of equal-sized groups or the size of each group**
rectangle: a quadrilateral with **2 pairs of opposite sides that are parallel and of equal length** and **4 right angles**
rectangular prism: a solid figure with **6 faces that are all rectangles**
remainder: the **amount leftover** when another whole group of the divisor cannot be made when dividing
rounding: to estimate the value of a number by determining the **nearest multiple of a specific place value**
row: a part of an array that **goes side to side**
square: a quadrilateral with **4 equal-length sides** and **4 right angles**
sum: the total when **2 or more numbers are added**
tape diagram: a tool that shows the relationship between quantities, represented by **rectangles placed side by side**
tenth: the base-ten place value unit **equal to 1/10** (one tenth in standard form is **.1**)
thousandth: the base-ten place value unit **equal to 1/1,000** (one thousandth in standard form is **.001**)
ton: a unit of weight in the U.S. customary measurement system (**1 ton is equal to 2,000 pounds**)
trapezoid: a quadrilateral with **at least 1 pair of opposite sides that are parallel**
unit fraction: a number that describes **exactly 1 part of a whole** that has been partitioned into **equal parts**
vertex: the point where the **adjacent sides of a shape meet**, **2 or more rays of an angle meet**, or **the edges of a solid figure meet** (plural: vertices)
volume: the amount of **space a three-dimensional figure takes up**
x coordinate: the first number in an ordered pair, indicating the **horizontal distance along the x-axis** from the origin at **(0,0)**
y coordinate: the second number in an ordered pair, indicating the **vertical distance along the y-axis** from the origin at **(0,0)**
